Markopoulos"}], "abstract": "The learning rate (LR) critically shapes the con-vergence and performance of machine learning models, yet traditional adaptive strategies often rely on manually tuned initializations and optimizer-specific designs, constraining their flexibility. This paper presents LG-XLR, a novel, fully automated, and optimizer-agnostic framework for dynamic LR adaptation, guided by real-time loss trends. Our approach hinges on two innovations: (1) loss-guided adaptation, where training and validation loss changes are monitored at each epoch to steer LR updates, and (2) an exponential LR range exploration that dynamically adjusts bounds without predefined schedules or initial guesses. By refining the LR range based on these loss-driven insights, our method exhibits stable convergence, mitigates overfitting, and eliminates task-specific tuning. Compatible with any gradient-based optimizer, it adapts seamlessly across models, datasets, and training scenarios. Experiments on CIFAR-10 image classification show consistent generalization (82-84% test accuracy) and faster convergence (25\u201342 epochs to 80% accuracy) across five optimizers, outperforming baselines like CLR and LRTuner in versatility and efficiency."}}, {"citingPaper": {"paperId": "e2e78e43c8b8de617b79b5e967561a8e9c8c37e3", "externalIds": {"DBLP": "conf/nips/JinHCCG22", "DOI": "10.52202/068431-2649", "CorpusId": 258509651}, "url": "https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/e2e78e43c8b8de617b79b5e967561a8e9c8c37e3", "title": "Revisit last-iterate convergence of mSGD under milder requirement on step size", "venue": "Neural Information Processing Systems", "year": 2022, "citationCount": 7, "openAccessPdf": {"url": "", "status": "CLOSED", "license": null, "disclaimer": "Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.52202/068431-2649?email=<INSERT_YOUR_EMAIL> or https://doi.org/10.52202/068431-2649, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Gupta"}], "abstract": "Understanding convergence of stochastic gradient descent (SGD) based optimization algorithms can help deal with enormous machine learning problems. To ensure last-iterate convergence of SGD and momentum-based SGD (mSGD), the existing studies usually constrain the step size \u03f5 n to decay as (cid:80) + \u221e n =1 \u03f5 2 n < + \u221e , which however is rather conservative and may lead to slow convergence in the early stage of the iteration. In this paper, we relax this requirement by studying an alternate step size for the mSGD. First, we relax the requirement of the decay on step size to (cid:80) + \u221e n =1 \u03f5 2+ \u03b7 0 n < + \u221e (0 \u2264 \u03b7 0 < 1 / 2) . This implies that a larger step size, such as \u03f5 n = 1 \u221a n can be utilized for accelerating the mSGD in the early stage. Under this new step size and some common conditions, we prove that the gradient norm of mSGD for a class of non-convex loss functions asymptotically decays to zero. In addition, we show that this step size can indeed help make the iterates of mSGD converge into a neighborhood of the stationary points quicker in the early stage. Finally, we establish the convergence of mSGD under a constant step size \u03f5 n \u2261 \u03f5 > 0 by removing a common requirement in the literature on strong convexity of the loss functions. Some experiments are given to illustrate the developed results."}}]}
